easy.def: A sickness where the body cannot use sugar well.
examples: My uncle has diabetes.
People with diabetes watch what they eat.
The nurse told us about diabetes.

examples: People with diabetes check the sugar in their blood with a tiny test.
My neighbor has diabetes, so she is careful about sweet foods.

easy.def: To find out what is wrong when someone is sick.
examples: The doctor will diagnose me.
She diagnosed the cause.
A mechanic can diagnose a car problem.

more.def: To find out what illness or problem someone or something has by checking it carefully.
examples: The doctor diagnosed the problem as a cold.
The vet diagnosed a sore paw on the dog.

easy.def: A round face with numbers or a knob you turn.
examples: The clock has a dial.

The dial shows the speed.

more.def: A round part with marks or numbers that shows a measurement, or a knob that you turn.
examples: The dial on the oven shows the heat.
He turned the radio dial to find a song.

easy.def: To call someone on a phone.

He dialed his friend.

more.def: To call a number on a telephone.

easy.def: A talk between two or more people.

more.def: The words that people in a story, play or movie say to each other.

easy.def: A clear, hard jewel.

Draw a diamond on your paper.

more.def: A group of things set out for people to look at.
examples: The window display had a toy train.
The fireworks display lit up the sky.
The science fair had a display of volcanoes.

easy.def: Getting rid of something.
examples: The disposal of trash is important.
The trash disposal is outside.
A food disposal.

more.def: The act of throwing away or getting rid of something.
examples: Safe disposal of old paint is important.
The town has a waste disposal plant.
The sink has a garbage disposal.

easy.def: To throw away.
examples: I dispose of trash.
Dispose of the waste.
They disposed of the old tires.

more.def: To get rid of something by throwing it away.
examples: I disposed of the empty bottles.
Dispose of the trash in the bin.
They disposed of the old tires properly.

easy.def: To not pay attention to something.
examples: Please disregard the first sentence.
He disregarded the sign.
They disregarded the rules.

more.def: To ignore something or treat it as not important.
examples: Please disregard my last message, because it was a mistake.
He disregarded the sign and walked on the grass.
The driver disregarded the speed limit.

easy.def: Not showing respect.
examples: Talking back shows disrespect.
He showed disrespect.
Disrespect hurts.

more.def: Rude behavior that shows you do not care about someone's feelings.
examples: Talking back to a teacher is disrespect.
He showed disrespect by laughing at her.
The coach did not accept disrespect.

easy.def: To interrupt something so that it cannot go on as planned.
examples: The noise disrupted my nap.
A noise disrupted class.
Do not disrupt the show.

more.def: To break in on something so that it stops or is thrown off.
examples: The storm disrupted the game.
A loud noise disrupted the class.
Please do not disrupt the show with your talking.

easy.def: To mix into a liquid and seem to disappear.
examples: Sugar dissolves in water.
The salt dissolved.
The tablet dissolves.

more.def: To mix completely into a liquid so that it cannot be seen.
examples: Sugar dissolves in hot tea.
The salt dissolved in the water.
The tablet dissolved in a glass of water.

easy.def: How far it is from one place to another.
examples: The distance to school is short.
We can see the hills in the distance.
I can throw the ball a long distance.

more.def: The amount of space between two places or things.
examples: The distance between our town and the ocean is two hundred miles.
The runners trained to race a distance of five miles.
From a distance, the two houses look exactly the same.

easy.def: Far away.
examples: The hills are distant.
I heard a distant sound.
A distant star.

more.def: Far away in space or time.
examples: We saw the distant hills through the haze.
A distant train whistle blew.
That happened in the distant past.

easy.def: Clear and easy to tell apart.
examples: I heard a distinct sound.
The two songs are distinct.
She has a distinct voice.

more.def: Clearly different from others, or easy to see, hear or notice.
examples: The two birds have distinct songs, so you can tell them apart in the dark.
The cat's footprints were distinct in the fresh snow.
Each flavor of ice cream has a distinct taste.

easy.def: A difference between two things.
examples: There is a distinction between day and night.
Can you see the distinction?
The distinction is small.

more.def: A clear difference between two things.
examples: There is a distinction between a frog and a toad.
Can you see the distinction between the two colors?
The teacher explained the distinction between a fact and an opinion.

easy.def: A special honor.
examples: She graduated with distinction.
It is a distinction to win.
The soldier earned a distinction.

more.def: Special praise or honor for doing something very well.
examples: She graduated from school with distinction.
It is a great distinction to win the gold medal.
The scientist earned the distinction of a famous prize.

easy.def: To tell things apart.
examples: I can distinguish the twins.
She can distinguish red from green.
How do you distinguish them?

more.def: To see or hear the difference between two things.
examples: I can distinguish the twins by their voices.
Birdwatchers distinguish species by their songs.
The dog can distinguish many scents.

easy.def: Famous and respected.
examples: The distinguished guest spoke.
He is a distinguished doctor.
A distinguished scientist.

more.def: Famous and respected because of great success.
examples: The distinguished guest gave a speech.
He is a distinguished doctor with many honors.
A distinguished scientist visited our school.

easy.def: To take someone's attention away from something.
examples: Noise can distract me.
The toy distracted the baby.
Do not distract the driver.

more.def: To pull someone's attention away from what they are doing.
examples: The loud noise distracted me from my work.
A toy distracted the baby from crying.
Please do not distract the bus driver.

easy.def: Something that takes your attention away.
examples: The noise was a distraction.
The toy is a distraction.
I need no distractions.

more.def: Something that turns your attention away from what you are doing.
examples: The loud noise was a distraction.
Turn off the TV to avoid distractions.
The butterfly was a nice distraction.

easy.def: Great worry or pain.
examples: The kitten was in distress.
She cried in distress.
The ship sent a signal of distress.

more.def: A state of great worry, pain or trouble.
examples: The kitten was in distress, stuck in the tree.
She cried in distress when she lost her toy.
The ship sent out a signal of distress.

easy.def: To give out things to many people.
examples: The teacher distributes the papers.
We distributed flyers.
Mom distributed the snacks.

more.def: To hand out or share something among many people.
examples: The teacher distributed the papers to the class.
We distributed flyers about the school fair.
Volunteers distributed food to families in need.

easy.def: Giving out things to many people.
examples: The distribution of books was fun.
The teacher did the distribution.
We helped with the distribution of food.

more.def: The act of giving out or spreading something among many people or places.
examples: The distribution of food to families was organized by the town volunteers.
The teacher handled the distribution of paper to every desk.
The map shows the distribution of rain across the country.

easy.def: A part of a town or country.
examples: Our school district has ten schools.
The district is near the river.
The shopping district is busy.

more.def: A part of a town, city or country, set apart for a purpose.
examples: Several schools in the district share a bus system.
The shopping district is full of stores.
The district around the old market is very busy.

easy.def: To bother someone or break their quiet.
examples: Do not disturb the baby.
The noise disturbed me.
Please do not disturb the sleeping cat.

more.def: To interrupt someone or to spoil the quiet or calm of something.
examples: Please do not disturb the baby while she sleeps.
The loud music disturbed our reading.
Do not disturb the nest in the tree.

easy.def: Something that stops people from being quiet or calm.
examples: The loud noise was a disturbance.
There was a disturbance outside.
Please, no disturbance.

more.def: Something that interrupts or upsets a quiet, calm or normal situation.
examples: A loud siren outside caused a disturbance in the library.
The storm caused a disturbance in the weather all across the state.
Scientists measure any disturbance in the ground after an earthquake.

easy.def: Upsetting.
examples: The news was disturbing.
A disturbing noise came.
It was disturbing to see.

more.def: Making you feel worried or upset.
examples: The disturbing news made her sad.
A disturbing noise came from the cellar.
It was disturbing to see the empty nest.

easy.def: A long, narrow hole in the ground.
examples: Water ran in the ditch.
The ball rolled into a ditch.
We jumped over the ditch.

more.def: A long, narrow channel dug in the ground, often to carry water away.
examples: Rainwater flowed along the ditch beside the road.
The workers dug a ditch for the pipe.
The ball rolled into the ditch.

easy.def: To jump into water head first.
examples: I dive into the pool.
She dove off the board.
The seal dived.

more.def: To jump into water with your head first, or to go deep under water.
examples: She dived into the pool with a splash.
The seal dove deep under the waves.
The swimmers dove for coins at the bottom.

easy.def: A person who swims under the water.
examples: The diver swam down.
A diver found a shell.
The diver wore a mask.

more.def: A person who swims deep under the water, or who dives from a high board.
examples: The diver swam down to look at the coral reef.
A diver found an old coin on the ocean floor.
The diver did two flips before she hit the water.

easy.def: To make something go a different way.
examples: The workers diverted the traffic.
He diverted the water.
Divert the river.

more.def: To make something turn or go in a different direction, or to turn attention away from something.
examples: The workers diverted traffic onto a side street while they fixed the road.
Farmers diverted the stream to water their fields.
The clown's funny hat diverted our attention from the magic trick.

easy.def: To split something into parts.
examples: Divide the cake.
We divided the candy.
The river divides the town.

more.def: To split something into parts or groups, or to do division in math.
examples: Divide the pizza into eight slices.
Ten divided by two is five.
The river divides the town in two.

easy.def: Coming from God, or wonderful.
examples: The song was divine.
The cake tasted divine.
The temple felt divine.

more.def: Having to do with God or a god, or so wonderful that it seems heavenly.
examples: In the story, the king asked for divine help.
The cake tasted absolutely divine.
The singer's voice sounded divine.

easy.def: Splitting a number into equal groups.
examples: We learned division in math.
Division is the opposite of multiplication.
Six divided by two is a division.

more.def: The act of splitting a number into equal parts in math, or of separating something into parts.
examples: In math class we practiced long division.
The division of the cake gave everyone a fair slice.
A fence made a clear division between the two yards.

easy.def: When two married people end their marriage.
examples: His parents got a divorce.
A divorce can be hard.
Her parents had a divorce.

more.def: The legal ending of a marriage.
examples: His parents got a divorce last year.
A divorce can be hard for a family.
The judge granted the divorce.

easy.def: Feeling like the room is spinning.
examples: I feel dizzy.
The ride made me dizzy.
I spun around and got dizzy.

more.def: Feeling unsteady, as if everything is spinning around you.
examples: I felt dizzy after spinning in circles.
The roller coaster made her dizzy.
He sat down because he felt dizzy.
